title: Lazard presentation of flat modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module such that $-\otimes_R M$ preserves short exact sequences of $R$-modules. There exist a small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$, an $I$-indexed system of $R$-modules $F_i$ with transition maps $F_i\to F_j$ for $i\le j$, and compatible maps $F_i\to M$, such that each $F_i$ is isomorphic to $R^{r_i}$ for some finite integer $r_i\ge0$, and the induced map $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}F_i\longrightarrow M$ is an isomorphism of $R$-modules; the colimit is that of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 058G (theorem-lazard), forward direction for flat modules

proof.text: Apply preservation of short exact sequences to an injective linear map f:A → B followed by the quotient B/range(f). The injectivity clause and Mathlib Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap give flatness in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

Let C have objects (n,p) with n a natural number and p:ULift(R^n) → M linear, and arrows the linear maps commuting with p. Objects and arrows are in the universe max(u,v). C is nonempty by the zero module. Direct sums, reidentified with coordinate modules by a finite basis, give common successors. For parallel arrows f,g:i → j, we have p_j(f-g)=0. The finite-relation factorization consequence of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion], Mathlib Module.Flat.exists_factorization_of_comp_eq_zero_of_free (Stacks 058D), gives p_j=y a with a(f-g)=0 and a landing in a finite free module. Thus a defines an arrow from j equalizing f and g. Consequently C is filtered.

source.place: Tag 058D (lemma-flat-factors-free), finite free factorization of a map annihilating a finite free relation module

proof.text: The forgetful functor C → Mod_R has its canonical cocone with vertex M. Prove it colimiting in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given a compatible cocone s, define u(m) as the value of s on the basis vector of the rank-one object p_m:R → M sending 1 to m. For every p_i:F_i → M and vector x, the linear map R → F_i sending 1 to x is an arrow p_(p_i(x)) → i, so compatibility gives u(p_i(x))=s_i(x). To prove additivity choose a common successor of p_a and p_b, with vectors x,y mapping to a,b. The formula on x,y,x+y proves u(a+b)=u(a)+u(b). The same formula in p_a on 1 and r gives u(ra)=r u(a). This defines a linear map, the formula proves all cocone equations, and rank-one objects prove uniqueness. No flatness is needed for this universal property.

Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.exists_directed (Stacks Categories 0032) to C, obtaining a nonempty directed partial order I in the same universe and a final functor G:I → C. Restrict the canonical cocone along G. Mathlib Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv transports the universal property from the previous step, so the restricted cocone is colimiting. Each object is ULift(R^n), linearly equivalent to Fin n → R by ULift.moduleEquiv followed by Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite. Uniqueness of colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] shows that colimit.desc is an isomorphism. These are all clauses of the original statement.
